newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa critical, pacemaker reprogrammed.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa critical, pacemaker reprogrammed.

text.p: Mother Teresa, fighting heart, kidney and lung problems, was in critical condition on Sunday following coronary artery surgery, her chief doctor said.
Dr D.P. Shetty said the 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun's heart pacemaker, fitted in 1989, had been reprogrammed to boost cardiac output to allow her kidneys to function better.
"She is still critically ill. You have to understand she has got a problem with her heart, kidney and lung," he said.
But he told reporters: "Mother is not in renal failure."
"We are trying to take care of everything. She is stable," added Shetty, who heads Mother Teresa's medical team at the B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre in Calcutta, eastern India.
Clinic administrator A.K. Chatterjee said earlier: "Mother is conscious and she spoke to medical staff."
Doctors said long-standing lung and renal problems could complicate her heart condition and recovery.
Mother Teresa, known as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her devotion to the poor, destitute and dying, had surgery on Friday to clear two coronary artery blockages.
Chatterjee said the renal and lung problems had forced doctors to delay treatment to correct an irregular heart rhythm.
A regular evening bulletin said: "Mother Teresa's condition is unchanged since the morning report. Physicians continue to monitor all her parameters very closely."
A midday bulletin said she remained in critical condition and her heart rhythm was still irregular. An earlier one said she was stable, comfortable and cheerful.
"We have reprogrammed the pacemaker to increase her cardiac output so that her kidney can work better," Shetty said.
"Her urine output is low, which is probably due to dehydration, low water content in her body. We are correcting that.
"We have taken care of her kidney and other parts of her body," he added.
Chatterjee said Mother Teresa, the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner, had chicken soup and fruit for lunch.
He said she had suffered from renal problems for the past two months and was receiving medication for them.
Chatterjee described the lung problem as chronic.
"At the age of 86 any problem is serious," he added.
On Saturday, American doctor Patricia Aubanel, another member of the medical team, said Mother Teresa had developed signs of bronchial pneumonia, which was being treated.
Shetty said early on Sunday that doctors were trying to correct with drugs her arrhythmia, or irregular heart rhythm.
"We are trying to correct her arrhythmia with medicine and we will watch her for two or three days.
"If it does not work, then only we have to go for mild electric shock or the mechanical cardioversion," he added.
Aubanel, who treated Mother Teresa in California in 1991, said cardioversion treatment for her arrhythmia was essential.
Mother Teresa, born of Albanian parents as Gonxhe Bojaxhi, was moved to the Birla clinic last Tuesday after entering the nearby Woodlands Nursing Home on November 22.
Nuns at the Calcutta headquarters of her Missionaries of Charity order prayed for her recovery on Sunday in a meeting that also included Hindus, Moslems, Sikhs and Buddhists.
